question.text: Lotus Capital AIF, a SEBI-registered Category II fund structured as a determinate, irrevocable contributory trust, earns INR 40 crore of long-term capital gains on the exit from an unlisted portfolio company during FY 2025-26. Under Section 115UB read with Section 10(23FBA) of the ITA, how is this income taxed?

answer.text: Taxed at the fund level at MMR (39% effective) because AIFs are assessed as AOPs.
Taxed at the fund level at 12.5% LTCG rate and then distributed net of tax to unitholders without any further tax in investor hands.
Taxed at 20% STCG rate at the fund level since the AIF is the direct seller of the shares.
Exempt in the fund's hands; taxed directly in the hands of the unitholders as LTCG on unlisted shares at 12.5% plus surcharge and cess.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 115UB read with Section 10(23FBA) accords pass-through status to Category I and II AIFs for all income OTHER than business income. The INR 40 crore LTCG is exempt at the fund level and flows through to unitholders retaining its character as LTCG on unlisted shares. Each unitholder is taxed at 12.5% (plus surcharge capped at 15% on LTCG and cess) on their pro-rata share. No tax is levied at the fund level. **The Trap:** Option A is the Cat III fund-level MMR treatment — which does not apply to Cat I/II. Option C invents a fund-level capital gains tax that doesn't exist under the pass-through regime. Option D misclassifies LTCG as STCG and ignores pass-through altogether. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the same Section 115UB pass-through but across ALL AIF categories (including the Cat III MMR carve-out). XIX-E (when it arrives) will test fund-level MMR for Cat III AOPs. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests this from a client-advisory angle — explaining TDS certificates to LPs. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** As a Cat I/II Manager, your LP onboarding deck and PPM 'Taxation' chapter must clearly disclose that pass-through preserves CHARACTER of income. A family-office LP will model LTCG differently from interest, so give them Form 64C-equivalent projections during fund-raising so they can size their ticket after-tax.
